long_biography.plain_text:
Russian Product took shape in 1996 when several food-manufacturing businesses were brought together under one company. Olga Mirimskaya led the group as a co-owner and board chair, extending its reach from dry groceries into coffee and beverages. A new full-cycle coffee plant showed her preference for building capabilities internally when specialist production technology was difficult to acquire.

Her management approach paired central control of major investment decisions with considerable authority for specialist executives. In a later operating cycle, she described reorganising teams, expanding online sales and using automation to link production, logistics and management. Those projects illustrate a career built around combining mature factories, consumer brands and new systems into a broader packaged-food platform.
